The best place to start is the **copyright page**, usually on the back of the title page.

## 5\. Understand the difference

| Term | Meaning |
|--------|--------|
| First edition | First published edition of the work |
| First printing | First batch printed of that edition |
| First edition, second printing | Same edition, but printed again |
| Revised edition | Updated or changed edition |
| Book club edition | Separate edition, often less collectible |


If you're interested in book collecting or resale value, a first edition, first printing is often the copy collectors want most.

Identifying a **first edition book** can be relatively easy with modern books, but older and collectible books require a little detective work.

| Number line | Meaning |

For collectible books, examine\:

- Original dust jacket.
- Original price printed on the inside flap.
- Publisher's logo and binding.
- Any distinctive printing errors or corrected text.

Collectors sometimes use these details, called *points of issue*, to distinguish an original first printing from later copies. If you have a book you're curious about, send me\:
